# Global footprints, government conditions and economic questions

## Start with a question the measurements can answer

The global workspace is a new lens on the retained resource/ownership/environment system. Ask how production emissions are attributed to resident economies, which origins are assigned to final demand, what appears in economic accounts, and which government conditions coincide with observed trade. Each panel preserves its own source period and boundary. A map can reveal an association worth investigating; a causal explanation needs a study design.

## Read the footprint maps

**Production** is the OECD residence-principle national greenhouse-gas estimate; **final demand** assigns emissions across production origins to a consuming economy. Both national totals include direct households. These published model-based estimates differ from territorial inventories and from retained EPA reporting populations. CO2e means carbon dioxide equivalent; units retain the publisher’s equivalence convention.

Absolute maps use **million tonnes CO2e**. Per-person maps use the publisher’s **tonnes CO2e per person**, rather than an inferred population join. Production and final-demand maps share one fixed scale through actual source years. Changing country centers the selected map boundary; Reset world view restores all geography. The timeline contains 28 actual years, 1995–2022. There is no extrapolation to 2026.

**Gross embodied imports/exports** can count emissions more than once as intermediates cross borders. **Foreign origins in final demand** instead allocate production-origin emissions to a consuming account. The origin map uses allocation arcs; it supplies no physical route, facility shipment, atmospheric transport or elapsed transit time. Domestic origin remains separate. Source rounding can leave residuals; zeros and missing data retain different meanings.

The primary map comprises 80 named economies plus a rest-of-world account. Eighteen overlapping aggregates remain selectable references, outside non-overlapping totals and bilateral origin edges. Not every source account has a native map boundary; all rows remain accessible in tables/evidence.

## Ask who benefits and who bears impacts with explicit proxies

The economic comparison defaults to the retained 50-industry whole-economy value-added sum and complete employee-compensation sum. It also allows industry detail in 2020–2022. Employee compensation is unavailable as a complete total when any retained industry lacks a value. Current million U.S. dollars are neither real purchasing power nor household welfare. National IOT compensation and global ICIO value added are separate harmonized sources; their differences are not forced away.

These accounts help locate recorded economic activity and labor compensation. They do not establish a particular commodity’s profits, household incidence, resource rents, tax benefit or owner’s receipts. Likewise, production accounts attribute estimated emissions to resident producing economies; they do not establish local exposure, health harm or climate damage. Those outcomes require compatible household, fiscal, price, exposure and impact data. Retained facility/owner evidence remains available without allocating a national footprint to a mine, company or Virginia.

For example, U.S. 2022 source totals are 6,305.691 million tonnes for production and 7,512.679 for final demand. This difference identifies a national accounting contrast. It does not establish who personally gained or lost from trade. The complete raw dimensions and country history accompany the view.

## Government conditions, legal references and observed trade

The policy selector provides eight different tariff measures: applied weighted/simple, most-favoured-nation weighted/simple, applied weighted manufactured/primary products, bound simple and binding coverage. A bound tariff is a committed ceiling. Binding coverage is a percentage of tariff lines with commitments, rather than a tariff rate. National averages cannot specify coal or pharmaceutical tariffs for an individual bilateral shipment; product mix can also change an import-weighted average.

Merchandise imports/exports remain **current U.S. dollars** and separate observed outcomes. Governance choices are **government effectiveness, regulatory quality and political stability**, from the WGI 2026 update. They use absolute 0–100 scores with the publisher’s 90% score intervals. Statistical-unit estimates and standard errors are retained separately. These perception-based measures are context, not an objective all-government-impact index.

WTO agreement records preserve signature, notification, goods/services entry, inactive and change dates as different event types. Current party lists are not projected backward or expanded into guessed historical bloc membership. Quantitative-restriction records retain exact HS revision, reported product lines, directions, partner exceptions, legal references and date fields. Notifications are incomplete and are not a complete inventory of sanctions, subsidies, export controls, SPS/TBT rules or customs administration. No record does not mean no policy.

On a captured flow, import context belongs to an exact destination country and export context to an exact origin country. Domestic links get no international tariff. Unknown country identities stay unmapped. Policy and flow years remain separately labeled; a country reference is not proof of product/partner legal applicability.

An acquired-source disagreement remains visible for U.S. 2019 applied tariffs. The WDI weighted 13.78%/simple 8.7% differ from the official WITS summary’s 1.58/2.94. Original observations and references remain in evidence, but those points are unavailable in comparative maps/history. No preferred substitute was silently chosen. See the source guide for the full reconciliation limits.

## Connect evidence to an economic assessment

1. Start in Goods, sites & ownership and capture a dated resource selection if useful. Virginia coal receipts and Norfolk port exports remain useful local-to-global entry points.
2. In Global footprints & trade policy, select the economy/year/measure for each lens. Choose the economic comparison’s own year and whole-economy or industry scope.
3. Use **Consider in the economic model workspace**. The context accompanies the existing country-industry monetary model. Its model country, industry, year and demand change remain independently specified.
4. Export economic evidence. The server re-reads installed sources from the selections; browser-supplied totals, rates and relationship claims do not become verified data. Footprint, policy, monetary and resource periods remain explicit. A captured whole-economy comparison does not become a guessed industry shock.

The existing monetary response is conditional on fixed input coefficients and prices. It does not estimate a tariff’s causal impact, substitution, prices, capacity constraints or household welfare. Comparative economic model assessment remains a research design rather than an automatic verdict.

**Environmental demand simulation is unavailable.** Exact 4,050-node direct-emissions vectors were acquired for 2020–2022 and their identifier mappings checked. When reconstructing official country final-demand industry footprints from the retained ICIO demand columns, 214 of 243 country-year checks exceeded the propagated rounding bound. The largest 2022 discrepancy was China +34.1564 million tonnes; the U.S. discrepancy was −5.7439. A small world residual does not resolve those country differences. No calibration was fitted. Official descriptive footprints and the original monetary model remain usable separately; the full diagnostic (research-edition file) records the gate.

## Export and continue analysis

PNG and SVG use fixed world framing and documented linear color scales. JSON companions preserve source evidence and selected settings. Signed net-import comparisons retain sign distinctions. CSV exports contain the selected year’s country rows plus a separate selected-country history; policy exports also contain its merchandise-trade history. Keep the companion files with a figure.

The existing numerical/statistical GUI remains available through Full data library. New global sources are explored in their own workspace; exported histories can be loaded into the existing custom-CSV workflow. Define experimental units, comparable years, outcome, denominators and model assumptions before interpreting correlation or regression. Time trends, reporting revisions and multiple comparisons can produce misleading associations. Bayesian inference requires a stated likelihood and prior, rather than a map-driven conclusion.

## Retained wealth and reproducibility

All 79 data files from 0.7 remain byte-identical; 1,940 numerical series in 16 collections and 341,857 observations remain available. Old editions and archives are preserved. Exact public-source downloads, normalized rows, deterministic rebuilders and readback receipts are in the two separate source packages. The workbench is a frozen local release, not a live monitoring service or public Civic Voice deployment.

Read footprint source definitions (research-edition file), government/trade definitions (research-edition file), connected reporting evidence (research-edition file), and the research framework (research-edition file). Examples: footprints (research-edition file) and government/trade (research-edition file).
